title: Euler operators detect all nonconstant p-basis coefficients of an element with zero differential
statement: Let p be prime and K/k an extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension] of characteristic p. Let B=kK^p be the intermediate field generated by the image of k and the p-th powers in K. Let t:I→K and assume the monomials t^F, indexed by finitely supported natural-valued exponents F with F_i<p, form a specified B-basis b of K. Assume a specified K-basis bd of the Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] has bd_i=dt_i. If da=0 and E is a nonzero bounded exponent, then the E-th coordinate b.repr(a)(E) is zero. No perfection assumption on k is required.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), proof of (2) implies (1), lines 11382-11394; its dual derivations and partial-derivative calculation, multiplied by t_i to give the Euler operator

proof.text: Fix a nonzero bounded exponent E and choose i with E_i > 0. Compose the universal derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] with the i-th coordinate of the assumed basis dt_j to obtain a k-derivation d_i satisfying d_i(t_j)=delta_ij.

The derivation d_i kills B=kK^p: it kills the base field, and Leibniz gives d_i(x^p)=p x^(p-1)d_i(x)=0. Addition, multiplication and the inverse rule preserve vanishing, so intermediate-field adjunction induction shows it kills every coefficient in B. Hence L_i(x)=t_i d_i(x) is B-linear.

Induct on the finite support of F. For F=0, d_i(1)=0. On adjoining a power t_j^n at a fresh index j, Leibniz and d_i(t_j)=delta_ij give L_i(t^F)=F_i t^F. In the j=i case use t_i*t_i^(n-1)=t_i^n for n>0; otherwise only the old product contributes. Thus L_i is diagonal on the assumed monomial basis.

Evaluate the B-linear maps coord_E composed with L_i and E_i times coord_E on each monomial basis vector. Both yield E_i times its E-th coordinate, so basis extensionality identifies the maps. Since D(a)=0, also L_i(a)=0, giving E_i*coord_E(a)=0. The scalar E_i is nonzero: otherwise characteristic p gives p dividing E_i, contradicting 0<E_i<p. Cancel it. For empty I there are no nonzero E; infinite I is covered by finite monomial supports.

lean.statement:
theorem pBasis_repr_eq_zero_of_D_eq_zero
    {k : Type u} {K : Type v} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] [CharP K p]
    {I : Type w} (t : I → K)
    (b : Module.Basis {E : I →₀ ℕ // ∀ i : I, E i < p}
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun x : K ↦ x ^ p))) K)
    (hb : ∀ E, b E = E.val.prod (fun i e ↦ t i ^ e))
    (bd : Module.Basis I K (KaehlerDifferential k K))
    (hbd : ∀ i, bd i = D k K (t i))
    (a : K) (ha : D k K a = 0)
    (E : {E : I →₀ ℕ // ∀ i : I, E i < p}) (hE : E.val ≠ 0) :
    b.repr a E = 0
